scenarios.command: three competing explanations for the Q3 fixture widget recall are filed at http://127.0.0.1:39553/recall-brief. for each explanation, read its dossier and the independent lab report it links, then tell me which explanation the lab evidence supports, with the measurement it rests on, and say what ruled out each of the other two

args.headline: Evaluate three recall explanations against lab evidence
args.objective: Read the recall brief and all three explanation dossiers with their linked lab reports, then report which explanation the lab evidence supports (with the key measurement) and what ruled out the other two.

args.observation: Lab report for the ceramic coating cure theory: cure times within tolerance on every recalled batch — theory NOT supported.
args.excerpt: Coating cure times were within tolerance on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported.

args.observation: Lab report for the bearing seat machining theory: bearing seats on every recalled batch machined 0.4 mm undersize — theory SUPPORTED.
args.excerpt: Bearing seats on every recalled batch were machined 0.4 mm undersize. This theory is SUPPORTED.

args.observation: Lab report for the packaging compression theory: packaging matched spec on every recalled batch — theory NOT supported.
args.excerpt: Packaging matched spec on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported.

args.subject: Bearing seat machining is the explanation for the Q3 fixture widget recall
args.detail: Lab found bearing seats machined 0.4 mm undersize on every recalled batch; the only SUPPORTED theory of the three.

metrics.answerText:
**Q3 fixture widget recall — verdict from the independent lab reports**

I read the recall brief and all three dossiers, each linking its own independent lab report:

- **Supported: bearing seat machining** — the lab found **bearing seats on every recalled batch were machined 0.4 mm undersize** ([lab report](http://127.0.0.2:34215/lab-bearing); [dossier](http://127.0.0.1:39553/theory-bearing))
- **Ruled out: ceramic coating cure** — coating cure times were **within tolerance on every recalled batch** ([lab report](http://127.0.0.2:34215/lab-coating); [dossier](http://127.0.0.1:39553/theory-coating))
- **Ruled out: packaging compression** — **packaging matched spec on every recalled batch** ([lab report](http://127.0.0.2:34215/lab-packaging); [dossier](http://127.0.0.1:39553/theory-packaging))

Exactly one of the three theories is supported by the lab evidence, consistent with the brief's note that only one would hold up.

scenarios.command: three consignments are listed at http://127.0.0.1:39553/consignment-index. each one's custody record is a chain of eight legs, and every leg links only the next one, so the seal number is on the last leg of each chain. for all three consignments, follow the whole chain and tell me the port it departed from and its container seal number

args.headline: Trace three consignment custody chains for departure port and seal number
args.objective: Follow each of the three consignments' eight-leg custody chains from the consignment index and report each consignment's departure port and container seal number (seal on the final leg).

args.escalation_reason: Each custody chain is 8 sequential pages; three chains exceed this run's remaining budget, so the two remaining independent chains (Marlin, Ibex) are delegated as parallel branches.
args.headline: Trace consignment custody chains: Falcon done, Marlin and Ibex in parallel
args.objective: Follow all three consignments' eight-leg custody chains and report each one's departure port and container seal number.

args.task: Trace the full 8-leg custody chain for Consignment Marlin. Start at http://127.0.0.1:39553/consign-marlin (leg 1 of 8). Each leg page contains exactly one link to the next leg (chains alternate between hosts 127.0.0.1:39553 and 127.0.0.2:34215). Leg 1 states the port the consignment departed from; leg 8 of 8 (the end of the chain, no further link) carries the container seal number. Report: (1) the departure port from leg 1, quoting the sentence, (2) the seal number from leg 8, quoting the sentence, and (3) the URLs of leg 1 and leg 8. Follow only the chain links; do not deviate.

Trace the full 8-leg custody chain for Consignment Ibex. Start at http://127.0.0.1:39553/consign-ibex (leg 1 of 8). Each leg page contains exactly one link to the next leg (chains alternate between hosts 127.0.0.1:39553 and 127.0.0.2:34215). Leg 1 states the port the consignment departed from; leg 8 of 8 (the end of the chain, no further link) carries the container seal number. Report: (1) the departure port from leg 1, quoting the sentence, (2) the seal number from leg 8, quoting the sentence, and (3) the URLs of leg 1 and leg 8. Follow only the chain links; do not deviate.

args.excerpt: Consignment Falcon departed Valdez on the first leg of its custody chain.
args.observation: Consignment Falcon departed from the port of Valdez (custody leg 1 of 8).

args.excerpt: Consignment Falcon arrived on the final leg under container seal SEAL-8123. This is the end of the chain.
args.observation: Consignment Falcon's container seal number is SEAL-8123 (custody leg 8 of 8, end of chain).
Consignment Marlin departed from the port of Ostend (custody leg 1 of 8, consign-marlin).
Consignment Marlin's container seal number is SEAL-4470 (custody leg 8 of 8, end of chain at custody-a5dw).
Consignment Ibex departed from the port of Trieste (custody leg 1 of 8, consign-ibex).
Consignment Ibex's container seal number is SEAL-9056 (custody leg 8 of 8, end of chain at custody-u3pk).

metrics.answerText:
## Consignment custody chains — all 3 followed through all 8 legs

| Consignment | Departed from (leg 1) | Container seal (leg 8, end of chain) |
|---|---|---|
| **Falcon** | Valdez | SEAL-8123 |
| **Marlin** | Ostend | SEAL-4470 |
| **Ibex** | Trieste | SEAL-9056 |

**How each chain ran** (legs alternate between the two record hosts, each page linking only the next leg):

- **Falcon** — [leg 1](http://127.0.0.1:39553/consign-falcon) "departed Valdez" → Northline Freight → Depot 12 → customs at Kettle Point → Weighbridge 3 → Harrow Surveying → Bay 18 → [leg 8](http://127.0.0.2:34215/custody-c8sy): "arrived on the final leg under container seal SEAL-8123. This is the end of the chain."
- **Marlin** — [leg 1](http://127.0.0.1:39553/consign-marlin) "departed Ostend" → Cormorant Haulage → Depot 27 → customs at Ravensgate → Weighbridge 9 → Lyle Marine Survey → Bay 4 → [leg 8](http://127.0.0.2:34215/custody-a5dw): "under container seal SEAL-4470. This is the end of the chain."
- **Ibex** — [leg 1](http://127.0.0.1:39553/consign-ibex) "departed Trieste" → Sablefish Lines → Depot 41 → customs at Marrow Crossing → Weighbridge 6 → Osprey Inspectorate → Bay 31 → [leg 8](http://127.0.0.2:34215/custody-u3pk): "under container seal SEAL-9056. This is the end of the chain."

Every leg of every chain was visited; ports come from each chain's first leg and seals from its final leg, exactly as the index described.
